body:
`get_metadata()` runs for every book in a sync page (up to SYNC_ITEM_LIMIT = 100, cps/kobo.py
~536) and calls `get_epub_layout(book, book_data)` (cps/kobo.py ~1143) -> `get_content_opf()`
(cps/epub_helper.py:62). That opens the book's zip, reads META-INF/container.xml, lxml-parses
it, reads the OPF, and lxml-parses that — per book, per sync page, uncached.

This app serves with gevent and WITHOUT monkey.patch_all(), so that I/O and parsing sits on the
request greenlet and blocks every other request for its duration.

Measured on a live 215-book instance (2026-08-05):

    warm page cache:  0.86s total, 4.0 ms/book  -> ~0.4s per 100-book sync page
    cold page cache:  ~60 ms/book               -> ~6s per 100-book sync page

Cold is the first sync after a restart, and the steady state for a library on NFS or a network
share (NETWORK_SHARE_MODE). Extrapolated to 5,000 books: ~20s warm, minutes cold, all of it
freezing the whole app. Plausible mechanism behind upstream CWA #1112 "Kobo sync times out on
large libraries".

The layout is an immutable property of the file, so it is trivially cacheable — key on
(book_id, format, mtime, size) so a replaced file invalidates naturally. Persisting it means a
device's daily sync does not re-pay after every restart.

Only the fixed-layout (pre-paginated) branch consumes the result, and 0 of 215 books on this
instance are fixed-layout — the common case pays the whole parse to learn nothing.
title: Kobo sync re-parses every book's EPUB container+OPF from disk on every sync page
